overview: The One Station One Product (OSOP) Scheme is an initiative by Indian Railways to promote local products and artisans by providing them a platform at railway stations to sell their goods. The scheme aims to enhance the livelihood of local communities, promote indigenous crafts, and improve passenger experience by offering region-specific products at stations. It supports the vision of 'Vocal for Local' and encourages entrepreneurship at the grassroots level.
objectives: To provide a sales outlet for local products at railway stations
To promote indigenous crafts and regional specialties
To enhance income opportunities for local artisans and self-help groups
To improve passenger experience by offering authentic local products
To support the 'Vocal for Local' initiative of the Government of India
To encourage entrepreneurship at the station level
To preserve and promote traditional art forms and culinary heritage
eligibility: Local artisans, self-help groups, cooperatives, NGOs, and MSMEs producing indigenous or region-specific products are eligible to participate in the OSOP scheme. Preference is given to products that reflect the cultural, culinary, or artisanal heritage of the station's locality.
benefits: Selected participants get allocated space at designated railway stations to display and sell their products. They benefit from increased visibility, direct access to a large passenger footfall, and opportunities for business growth. The scheme provides non-financial support such as training in packaging, branding, and customer service, along with facilitation for digital payments and marketing through Indian Railways' channels.
financial_support: The OSOP scheme does not provide direct financial subsidies or grants. Instead, it offers nominal or concessional licensing fees for stall allocation, with revenue sharing models where applicable. Indian Railways facilitates logistics and infrastructure support, but primary investment in product development and inventory is borne by the beneficiaries.
application_process: 1. Identify the nodal officer or station manager at the respective railway station. 2. Submit a proposal detailing the product, its local significance, production capacity, and business plan. 3. Provide samples and documentation such as business registration, GST details, and product photographs. 4. Await evaluation by the station-level committee. 5. Upon approval, sign an agreement for space allocation and comply with operational guidelines. 6. Begin operations after receiving clearance from railway authorities.
required_documents: Details of production process and raw materials
Identity and address proof of the applicant
Bank account details for revenue settlement
Any certifications related to product quality or origin (e.g., GI tag, FSSAI)
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year based on station availability and product suitability.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Railways, Government of India
contact_details: Email: railwayboard@indianrailways.gov.in | Helpline: 139 (Rail Madad) | Contact Us: https://indianrailways.gov.in/contactUs.html
caveats: Allocation of space is subject to availability and safety regulations at the station
Products must comply with food safety (FSSAI), quality, and legal standards where applicable
No prohibited or hazardous items can be sold under the scheme
Beneficiaries must maintain hygiene and adhere to station cleanliness norms
The railway administration reserves the right to terminate allocation in case of violations or complaints
